facts.text: Fuenlabrada’s name comes from the Spanish phrase “Fuente Labrada,” meaning a carved fountain.
Archaeologists have found evidence of human activity in the area dating back to the Paleolithic and Bronze Age.
During the Upper Middle Ages, nearby settlements such as Loranca, Albas and Fregacedos were already part of the municipality’s territory.
The first documented mention of Fuenlabrada appears in the 16th‑century Topographic Relations of Philip II.
By the late 19th century, Fuenlabrada was famous for its handmade rosquillas and buns, a local culinary specialty.
After suffering serious damage in the Spanish Civil War, the municipality received rebuilding aid from the Dirección General de Regiones Devastadas in the 1940s and 1950s.
